# Independent audit: compatible Minkowski interpolation and cap response

Audited source:
`candidate d9792f1ce8a8f405`,
all four sections. **PASS; no repair.** The source's exact verifier was
rerun: **1,334 exact checks PASS**.

The anchored inclusion in (2) follows from distributivity of finite
Minkowski sums and nonnegative scalar multiplication. It preserves the
actual fibers in the convex fiber hull; completeness and the stated
rank repair handle the integer-base realization. This is an exact
compatibility closure, not a statement about linearized responses.

For the two trapezoids, fixing `x1+x2=2x` makes the averaged roof loss
`1+x1-x`. Its minimum on the actual two bounded horizontal intervals is
`|x|`. The common lower endpoint is attainable and vertical convexity
fills the interval, proving the whole pentagon equality, not just its
upper boundary. Integrating `1+x`, `1-x`, and `|x|` on either half of
the top edge verifies every finite area/cap formula (4)--(5).

On the binary integer base, a finite exposing tilt isolates each fiber
without changing its continuous cap, while every ambient cap captures
at least its own trace. Thus mixed depth on each base equals ordinary
depth there. Central symmetry gives the asserted original global raw
maximum `2`, normalized value `3/10`, and the stated finite critical
cover. The other-base traces in the displayed caps are strictly empty;
the two additional opposite caps cover that base with strict mass
slack. The deformation of the other rectangle has exact area loss one.

The averaged row-loss vector is `(1,1)` with total loss three and hence
payment `1/10` per row. The actual Minkowski-interpolated pentagon has
row losses `(1/2,1/2)` and total loss two, giving `-1/10`. The separate
averaged-roof rectangle genuinely realizes the former linear response
and its normalized global depth strictly decreases. The pentagon's
negative fixed-cover response is correctly not called a global-depth
increase or an impossibility of some other convexification.

The support quotient at fixed normal `(eta,1)` has limits two on the
positive side and zero at and to the left of the top normal. Unit
normalization retains that discontinuity, so uniform convergence to a
continuous support derivative indeed fails. Finally, the mixed-volume
telescoping identity (11), including the factor `1/d` and its `d` terms,
gives linear TOTAL first variation under the source's explicit uniform
continuous-support-derivative hypothesis. It does not establish the
separate fixed-cap response closure, which is correctly retained as an
additional requirement.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
